objects.definition: typedef uint32_t avr_flashaddr_t;
objects.description: Typedef for flash address units in bytes used by the AVR simulator (program counter, code memory indexing).

objects.definition:
typedef uint8_t (*avr_io_read_t)(
		struct avr_t * avr,
		avr_io_addr_t addr,
		void * param);
objects.description: Function pointer type for IO read callbacks. Implementations should return the byte read from the given IO address for the specified AVR instance.

objects.definition:
typedef void (*avr_io_write_t)(
		struct avr_t * avr,
		avr_io_addr_t addr,
		uint8_t v,
		void * param);
objects.description: Function pointer type for IO write callbacks. Implementations should write value v to the given IO address for the specified AVR instance.

Holds trace-related debug data for the simulator when tracing is enabled (CONFIG_SIMAVR_TRACE). Tracks code lines, recent PCs/SPs, optional stack frames, and which registers were touched by the last instruction.

objects.definition:
typedef void (*avr_run_t)(
		struct avr_t * avr);
objects.description: Function pointer type for the core run loop implementation used by an avr_t instance.

Primary simulator state object for an AVR core. Holds device identity, memory sizes, runtime state, callbacks, IRQ pools, IO mapping, timers, interrupts, tracing, gdb hooks, VCD tracing, and code/data memory pointers. Must be initialized via avr_make_mcu_by_name/avr_init and reset via avr_reset before use.
Factory descriptor for a particular AVR device kind, including up to 4 alias names and a constructor that returns a new avr_t instance for that device.
Represents a symbol loaded from an ELF file with address, size, and a flexible array member for the symbol name string.

Base struct for simavr IO modules. Intended to be embedded as the first member of a module-specific struct so it can participate in the IO module chain. Holds back-pointers to the owning avr_t, IRQ metadata and array, and function pointers for reset, ioctl handling, and optional deallocation. External types avr_t, avr_irq_t, avr_io_addr_t, avr_io_read_t, and avr_io_write_t are referenced but defined elsewhere. Usage: module implementations should populate kind/irq fields as needed, implement reset/ioctl/dealloc callbacks, and link via next when registered. Construction/destruction are managed via the API functions in this header and the core; there is no standalone constructor for this struct in this header.

objects.definition: struct avr_irq_t;
objects.description: Forward declaration of the public IRQ structure used across the IRQ subsystem. The full definition appears later in this header. Used to declare pointers and function signatures before the complete type is defined.

Pool container that groups and manages a set of IRQs belonging to a device/AVR instance. Tracks the number of IRQs, their array, and a back-reference to the owning avr_t. Construction/initialization is typically done via avr_alloc_irq() or avr_init_irq() using a pointer to this pool.

Public IRQ structure representing a single interrupt signal endpoint. Holds metadata (name, id), current value, flags, a link to its owning pool, and a hook list for notifications/chaining. Instances are allocated/initialized via avr_alloc_irq() or avr_init_irq() and freed with avr_free_irq(). Flags are manipulated with avr_irq_get_flags()/avr_irq_set_flags(). Values are propagated with avr_raise_irq()/avr_raise_irq_float().

objects.definition:
typedef void (*avr_irq_notify_t)(
		struct avr_irq_t * irq,
		uint32_t value,
		void * param);
objects.description: Function pointer type for IRQ notification callbacks. Called when an IRQ is raised; receives the IRQ pointer, the new value, and a user-supplied parameter. Register/unregister via avr_irq_register_notify()/avr_irq_unregister_notify().

Represents a single AVR interrupt vector definition/state. Contains the vector number, regbit descriptors for enable and raised flags, optional PCINT alignment mask/shift, per-vector IRQ endpoints for pending/running signaling, and bitfields for scheduling/debug/sticky-flag behavior. Intended to be registered with the core and used by helper APIs to raise/clear and trace interrupts. Construction is typically by static or stack allocation and initialization of fields; ownership/registration handled by the interrupt table. Destruction details are not specified here.

objects.definition: DECLARE_FIFO(avr_int_vector_p, avr_int_pending, 64);
objects.description: Type generated by DECLARE_FIFO macro: a FIFO type for avr_int_vector_p elements with capacity 64 (power-of-two). Exact struct name and fields are macro-defined in fifo_declare.h; here the canonical pointer type is avr_int_pending_t *. Used by the interrupt table to queue pending vectors. Full definition not visible in this header.

Holds the global interrupt controller state for an AVR core: registered vector pointers (up to 64), count, a FIFO of pending vectors, a stack of running vectors with pointer, and global IRQ endpoints for pending/running statuses. Typically embedded in or owned by the core (struct avr_t) and initialized/reset via avr_interrupt_init/avr_interrupt_reset. Lifetime is managed with the core; direct construction is by allocation and field initialization, but API provides init/reset functions.

objects.definition:
typedef int (*avr_cmd_handler_t)(
		struct avr_t * avr,
		uint8_t v,
		void * param);
objects.description: Function pointer type for command handlers. Called when a command code is written to the configured IO address. Returns non-zero to indicate a multi-byte command sequence is ongoing; subsequent writes are dispatched to the same handler until it returns 0.
Entry representing a single registered command: a handler callback and an opaque parameter passed to the handler.
Table of registered commands for an AVR instance, including a fixed-size command array and a pointer to the handler of a currently pending multi-byte command sequence.

objects.definition:
typedef avr_cycle_count_t (*avr_cycle_timer_t)(
		struct avr_t * avr,
		avr_cycle_count_t when,
		void * param);
objects.description: Function pointer type for a cycle timer callback. The callback receives the AVR instance, the scheduled absolute cycle count, and a user parameter. It returns either 0 to clear the timer or a new absolute cycle count to reschedule the timer.

Node/slot in the cycle timer system. Holds a scheduled absolute cycle count, the callback to invoke, its parameter, and a next pointer for queue/list linkage. Used in free and active lists. Destruction and allocation are managed by the pool; users should not allocate directly.

Pool and queues for cycle timer slots. Contains a fixed array of slots and pointers to the head of the free list and the active (pending) list. Internally used by the simulator core to manage timers; not typically manipulated directly by users.

Dynamic argument-vector container holding a destructively tokenized command line. Fields: size (allocated byte size for this structure including flexible array), argc (number of tokens), line (mutable buffer containing the tokenized text, with delimiters replaced by NULs), argv (flexible array of char* pointers into line). Intended to be filled by argv_parse, which splits input into words and populates argc/argv. Caller manages memory for both the argv_t instance and the line buffer; no string duplication is performed.

objects.definition: struct elf_firmware_t;
objects.description: Incomplete forward declaration of a firmware descriptor used by sim_setup_firmware to return parsed ELF/HEX metadata and contents. The full structure definition is not present in this header; details such as fields and lifecycle are unknown here.

Linked-list node representing a contiguous chunk of firmware data loaded from an ELF; includes memory type, start address, sizes, next pointer, and a flexible-size data payload. The data array is effectively variable-length (size bytes). Unknowns: allocation and ownership semantics are not specified here—expect functions in the implementation to allocate and link these nodes.

objects.definition: enum mem_type { FLASH, DATA, EEPROM, FUSES, LOCK, UNKNOWN };
objects.description: Enumeration of memory segments used by AVR firmware images: program flash, data (SRAM), EEPROM, fuses, lock bits, and an unknown type.

Top-level container for parsed AVR ELF firmware metadata and contents, including MCU name, clocks and voltages, tracing configuration, external port states, command/console registers, flash base, and a linked list of data chunks. When ELF_SYMBOLS is enabled, holds symbol table pointers and DWARF filename. Must be zero-initialized before use; population is performed by elf_read_firmware and related routines.

Pointer to pointer type referenced when ELF_SYMBOLS is enabled. The underlying type is not defined in this header; it is declared elsewhere. This entry included only to note the alias requirement: however, since the base type is not defined here, no further details are available.

Bitmask-style enumeration of GDB breakpoint/watchpoint kinds used by the simulator: soft/hard breakpoints and write/read/access watchpoints. Intended for specifying and reporting watchpoint events to the GDB integration.
Represents a single VCD signal tracked by the module. Holds the IRQ line used as the data source/sink, a single-character VCD alias, the bit-width, and a human-readable name.
Log entry for a signal change. Records time (cycles for output, nanoseconds for input), the index of the signal, whether the signal is floating, and its value. Used internally and stored in a FIFO.

objects.definition: DECLARE_FIFO(avr_vcd_log_t, avr_vcd_fifo, 256);
objects.description: FIFO container type generated by DECLARE_FIFO macro to hold avr_vcd_log_t entries with capacity 256. Exact struct definition comes from fifo_declare.h and is not shown here.

Main VCD context for simavr. Manages input/output files, the list of tracked signals, time mapping, and a FIFO log of value changes. Can operate in output mode (recording IRQ changes) or input mode (replaying from a VCD).

Not defined in this header. avr_regbit_t is referenced throughout as a small descriptor for a bit-field in an AVR I/O register, with fields reg (uint16_t register address), bit (bit position), and mask (bit-width mask). Its actual definition is expected in sim_avr.h included above. Because it is only referenced and not defined here, details such as layout and construction semantics are inferred and not guaranteed.
Type used for counting CPU cycles in the simulator. It is referenced here but not defined in this header; its exact underlying type is unknown from this file.
Represents the AVR core/context, providing fields like frequency; referenced for time conversions. The struct is forward-declared via usage but not defined here; its layout is unknown from this file.

Type representing the simavr analog comparator peripheral instance. It embeds IO descriptor, multiplexer control bits, ADC/power flags, control/status register mappings, interrupt vector, runtime sampled input values, and linkage to a timer IRQ. Intended to be initialized with avr_acomp_init and then integrated into an avr_t simulator instance. Destruction/teardown details are not documented here.

Anonymous enum defining ADC-related IRQ indices for simavr. Values represent IRQ lines (millivolts for ADC inputs). Used as integral constants; not a named type. Note: As it's anonymous, the canonical pointer type is int * for the underlying enum type in C. Details about size follow compiler rules.

ADC multiplexer mode descriptor. Bitfields encode the mux kind (none/noise/single/diff/temp/ref/vcc/4), differential gain, differential source, and source channel index. Used to describe how the ADC input is selected.
Anonymous enum listing ADC mux kinds used in avr_adc_mux_t.kind. No named type; constants only.
Anonymous enum of ADC reference voltage selector codes/values. Used as constants to populate ref_values or configure reference selection. No named type.

objects.definition:
typedef enum {
	avr_adts_none = 0,
	avr_adts_free_running,
	avr_adts_analog_comparator_0,
	avr_adts_analog_comparator_1,
	avr_adts_analog_comparator_2,
	avr_adts_analog_comparator_3,
	avr_adts_external_interrupt_0,
	avr_adts_timer_0_compare_match_a,
	avr_adts_timer_0_compare_match_b,
	avr_adts_timer_0_overflow,
	avr_adts_timer_1_compare_match_b,
	avr_adts_timer_1_overflow,
	avr_adts_timer_1_capture_event,
	avr_adts_pin_change_interrupt,
	avr_adts_psc_module_0_sync_signal,
	avr_adts_psc_module_1_sync_signal,
	avr_adts_psc_module_2_sync_signal,
} avr_adts_type;
objects.description: Named enum describing ADC Auto Trigger Source (ADTS) selections available on various AVR cores. Values map ADTS mux codes to their trigger sources.

ADC peripheral model for simavr. Encapsulates register mirrors, bitfields, configuration, trigger selections, mux table, runtime state, and buffered result for the AVR ADC simulation. Depends on types from sim_avr.h (avr_io_t, avr_regbit_t, avr_int_vector_t).

Bit-bang interface state and configuration for simavr. Holds configuration (clock generation, polarity/phase, data order, buffer size), callback hooks for bit I/O and transfer completion, associated AVR instance, optional I/O pins, and internal buffer/counters. Used to perform generic bit-banged protocols (e.g., SPI-like, I2C-style when sharing pins).

EEPROM peripheral model for an AVR MCU within simavr. Holds IO header, backing byte array pointer, size, register addresses, control bits, and the ready interrupt vector. Used to emulate EEPROM read/write behavior and interrupts. Construction typically happens by embedding/initializing this inside an AVR core using the provided macros and calling avr_eeprom_init.

Descriptor for a contiguous EEPROM region: pointer to bytes, start offset, and size. Likely used with IOCTLs to get/set backing storage for the EEPROM peripheral. Exact semantics depend on surrounding API.

External interrupt controller/relay for AVR INT0..INT7 within simavr. Embeds a base avr_io_t and, per interrupt line, the sense-control bits, associated interrupt vector, and mapping to an I/O port pin. The strict_lvl_trig field enables repetitive triggering while the pin is held low. Construction and lifecycle are managed in the simulator core; initialize with avr_extint_init. Depends on types from sim_avr.h (avr_io_t, avr_regbit_t, avr_int_vector_t, avr_t).

Self-programming (SPM/LPM) subsystem state for an AVR core within simavr. Holds IO integration, temporary page buffers, page size, control/status regbits for self-programming operations, optional RWW and signature-read features, and the flash interrupt vector.

IOCTL helper structure used with AVR_IOCTL_IOPORT_GETIRQ_REGBIT to map a given register bit (avr_regbit_t) corresponding to PORT/PIN/DDR into the matching IRQ lines. Caller provides bit; callee fills irq[] with up to 8 irq pointers, NULL-terminated.
Bitfield structure returned by AVR_IOCTL_IOPORT_GETSTATE(<port-name>) describing the current state of an I/O port: name (letter), PORT register value, DDR register value, and PIN register value.

IOCTL argument structure for AVR_IOCTL_IOPORT_SET_EXTERNAL(<port-name>) to set default input behavior for a port: mask selects pins affected; value provides default levels when configured as inputs (e.g., pull configuration for simulation).
Simple pin descriptor packing a port letter and pin index into a 16-bit bitfield. Useful for APIs needing to reference a specific I/O pin.

Core I/O port descriptor for simavr. Holds register addresses (PORT, DDR, PIN), the port name, PCINT vector/mask, and mapping adjustments (mask/shift) for PCINT alignment. Tracks irq generation state and default external pull configuration for input mode. Used by avr_ioport_init to register and emulate a port.

Logical device model for an AVR LIN (Local Interconnect Network) controller within simavr. It embeds the generic I/O interface (avr_io_t), register addresses for LIN bit timing and baud rate registers, bitfields for enable/interrupt/status control, and an embedded UART model used when the LIN controller operates in UART mode. Intended to be initialized and registered with an avr_t instance via avr_lin_init. Destruction/teardown behavior is not defined in this header; ownership is typically by the parent avr_t simulation context.

SPI peripheral descriptor for simavr. Holds I/O registration, register addresses, control/status bit descriptors, and the SPI interrupt vector. Intended to be embedded in an AVR device model and initialized via avr_spi_init. Fields reference sim_avr types (avr_io_t, avr_regbit_t, avr_io_addr_t, avr_int_vector_t) defined elsewhere.
Waveform Generation Mode descriptor used by the timer to define TOP/BOTTOM, counter size, and mode kind. Packed into 32 bits using bitfields (8 bits each).

Comparator unit state for a timer channel (A/B/C). Holds interrupt vector, links to parent timer, OCR registers, compare output mode bits, output pin binding, accumulated compare timing, and force-compare control bit.

Core AVR timer peripheral model used by simavr. Encapsulates IO registration, mode configuration (WGM), clock selection and division, external clocking options, input capture, comparator channels, interrupt vectors, and overflow accounting/state.
Packed 32-bit bitfield layout for a TWI IRQ message: top-level fields encode message type (msg), 7-bit address (addr) and data byte, with an unused byte. Used inside IRQ payloads.
Wrapper for TWI IRQ value allowing access as a 32-bit integer (v) or as structured fields (twi). Used when sending/receiving TWI IRQ messages.
Simavr TWI (I2C) peripheral device instance. Holds IO register addresses, control/status bit descriptors, interrupt vector, and internal state for master/slave operation.

AVR UART peripheral model used by simavr. Encapsulates register addresses, control/status bits, interrupt vectors, an input FIFO, state counters, timing, and optional stdio buffering. Intended to be embedded in an MCU device model and initialized via avr_uart_init; macros AVR_UARTX_DECLARE/AVR_UART_DECLARE fill the register/bit mappings for specific chips.

I/O request descriptor for USB pipe transfers used with the AVR ioctl USB interface. Fields: pipe selects the endpoint/pipe, sz is the transfer size in bytes (input or output depending on operation), and buf points to the data buffer. Intended to be passed with AVR_IOCTL_USB_* requests. Error codes are indicated by AVR_IOCTL_USB_NAK/STALL, success by AVR_IOCTL_USB_OK.

Primary USB peripheral descriptor for a simulated AVR device in simavr. Embeds avr_io_t for integration with the I/O system, tracks configuration and register base addresses (r_usbcon, r_pllcsr), interrupt vectors (usb_com_vect, usb_gen_vect), and status bits (disabled in PRR, usbrf in MCUSR). The state pointer references an internal implementation structure (forward-declared elsewhere). Name holds a single-character identifier. Used to register and operate the USB module with the simulator.

objects.definition:
typedef struct avr_usi_t {
	avr_io_t	io;

	avr_io_addr_t	r_usicr;	// control register
	avr_io_addr_t	r_usisr;	// status register
	avr_io_addr_t	r_usidr;	// data register
	avr_io_addr_t	r_usibr;	// buffered data register

	avr_regbit_t 	usipf;		// stop condition flag
	avr_regbit_t 	usidc;		// data collision flag
	avr_regbit_t 	usiwm;		// wire mode
	avr_regbit_t 	usics;		// clock source
	avr_regbit_t 	usiclk;		// clock strobe
	avr_regbit_t 	usitc;		// clock toggle

	uint32_t		port_ioctl;	// ioctl to use to get port
	avr_regbit_t	pin_di;		// data in pin
	avr_regbit_t	pin_do;		// data out pin
	avr_regbit_t	pin_usck;	// clock pin

	avr_irq_t      *toggle_irq; // Clock pins IRQ

	avr_int_vector_t usi_start;	// start condition interrupt
	avr_int_vector_t usi_ovf;	// overflow interrupt

	uint8_t		clock_high;	// clock phase
	uint8_t		in_bit0;	// DI pin input value.
} avr_usi_t;
objects.description: USI (Universal Serial Interface) peripheral model for simavr. Holds register addresses, bitfields, pin mappings, IRQ handle, interrupt vectors, and internal state used to emulate the USI module on supported AVR devices.

State container for the AVR watchdog peripheral within simavr. Embeds IO registration, bitfields for control/status (reset flag, change enable, enable, prescaler bits), an interrupt vector, timing/cycle tracking, and a small reset context used to restore state across resets. Intended to be initialized and attached to an avr_t core.
Holds ANSI escape code strings (or similar) for colored terminal output. Provides three color/style entries: green, red, and normal (reset). Used for formatting debug/trace output in simavr.

Opaque type representing an AVR device kind/descriptor. This header only references it via extern variables and an extern array, but does not define the type. It is likely defined in another header (e.g., sim_core_config.h or a related module). Details such as fields, construction, and destruction are unknown from this file.

objects.definition: extern avr_kind_t * avr_kind[];
objects.description: Global null-terminated array of pointers to avr_kind_t instances, conditionally populated with the supported MCU variants compiled in. When AVR_KIND_DECL is defined in one translation unit, this header also provides the definition and initialization of the array with addresses of the extern avr_kind_t device descriptors and a terminating NULL.

These are extern declarations for specific AVR device kind descriptors, each of type avr_kind_t. They are conditionally declared based on build-time CONFIG_* macros and are later collected into the avr_kind[] registry. They are not separate types; they are aliases/names of avr_kind_t instances representing concrete MCU models.

functions.name: avr_make_mcu_by_name
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new AVR instance configured for the MCU identified by name. Used to obtain a simulator instance matching a specific AVR model.
requirements: name must be a valid MCU identifier supported by simavr (e.g., matches known device names/aliases).
Caller must check the return value for NULL to detect unknown/unsupported names or allocation failure.
The returned avr_t* should be initialized with avr_init() before running.

functions.name: avr_init
functions.description: Initializes a newly created AVR instance. Calls IO registers init() and then performs a reset on the core.
requirements: avr must be a non-NULL pointer obtained from avr_make_mcu_by_name() or avr_core_allocate().
Should be called once per avr instance before avr_run() or other runtime operations.
Caller should check the returned int for success/failure (exact return codes are unknown).

functions.name: avr_core_allocate
functions.signature: avr_t * avr_core_allocate(const avr_t * core, uint32_t coreLen)
functions.description: Allocates a mutable avr_t instance from a const core template. Intended for use by core implementations to create a working instance.
requirements: core must point to a valid core template object.
coreLen must be the size, in bytes, of the core template region to copy (must match the template type size).
Caller must check the return value for NULL on allocation failure.
The returned avr_t* should be initialized via avr_init().

functions.name: avr_reset
functions.description: Resets the AVR core and IO modules. Also uses avr->reset callback if set. Puts the simulator into the reset state (e.g., PC to reset vector, flags set).
requirements: avr must be a non-NULL initialized instance.
May be called to reinitialize state between runs; exact effects on attached devices depend on their reset behavior.

functions.name: avr_get_core_irq
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a core IRQ object identified by irq_no (e.g., AVR_CORE_BAD_OPCODE).
requirements: avr must be a non-NULL initialized instance.
irq_no must be a valid core IRQ number in the range [0, AVR_CORE_IRQ_COUNT-1].
Caller must check the returned pointer for NULL.

functions.name: avr_get_memory_irq
functions.signature: avr_irq_t * avr_get_memory_irq(avr_t * avr, uint16_t addr, int is16)
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a memory IRQ associated with the given memory address. Used to observe or drive memory access events.
requirements: avr must be a non-NULL initialized instance.
addr is the target memory address; valid ranges depend on the device’s memory map (unknown here).
is16 indicates whether the memory access is 16-bit (nonzero) or 8-bit (zero); exact semantics are not documented here.
Caller must check the returned pointer for NULL.

functions.name: avr_run
functions.description: Runs one simulator cycle for the AVR, sleeping if necessary based on timing. Intended to be called repeatedly in a loop to advance simulation.
requirements: avr must be a non-NULL initialized instance (avr_init() completed).
Caller should handle the return value (meaning of codes is not specified here).

functions.name: avr_terminate
functions.description: Finishes any pending operations and cleans up simulator state for the given instance (e.g., triggers custom deinitialization).
requirements: avr must be a non-NULL instance that has been initialized.
After termination, the instance should not be used unless reinitialized or recreated.

functions.name: avr_set_command_register
functions.description: Designates an IO register to receive simulator commands from AVR firmware. Uses ELF tags when available.
requirements: avr must be initialized.
addr must be a valid IO register address for the configured MCU.
Only needed if firmware communicates with the simulator via a command register.

functions.name: avr_set_console_register
functions.description: Sets the “console register” so writes from firmware to this IO address are printed on the simulator console without a UART.
requirements: avr must be initialized.
addr must be a valid IO register address for the configured MCU.

functions.name: avr_loadcode
functions.signature: void avr_loadcode(avr_t * avr, uint8_t * code, uint32_t size, avr_flashaddr_t address)
functions.description: Loads a block of bytes into the AVR’s flash memory starting at the given flash address. Typically used to load program code.
requirements: avr must be a non-NULL instance with flash allocated for the MCU.
code must be a valid pointer to at least size bytes when size > 0.
address and size must fit within the device’s flash (address + size must not exceed avr->flashend + 1).
Behavior for overlapping previous contents and unaligned addresses is device/simulator-defined (not specified here).

functions.name: avr_core_watch_write
functions.signature: void avr_core_watch_write(avr_t *avr, uint16_t addr, uint8_t v)
functions.description: Writes a byte to the AVR data space with watchpoint support so debuggers can observe the write. Used by IO modules and the core.
requirements: avr must be initialized.
addr must be a valid data-space address (general purpose registers, IO registers, or SRAM) for the device; exact valid range is device-specific.
v is written as a single byte.

functions.name: avr_core_watch_read
functions.description: Reads a byte from the AVR data space with watchpoint support so debuggers can observe the read. Used by IO modules and the core.
requirements: avr must be initialized.
addr must be a valid data-space address (general purpose registers, IO registers, or SRAM) for the device; exact valid range is device-specific.

functions.name: avr_sadly_crashed
functions.description: Notifies the simulator that the core crashed (e.g., watchdog fired). May activate the GDB server depending on configuration.
requirements: avr must be initialized.
signal indicates the crash reason; the exact encoding is not specified here.
If GDB auto-start on crash is disabled, the simulator may exit; behavior is configuration-dependent.

functions.name: avr_global_logger
functions.signature: void avr_global_logger(struct avr_t* avr, const int level, const char * format, ...)
functions.description: Logs a message using the current global logger. Level corresponds to the LOG_* levels. Variadic arguments follow printf-style formatting.
requirements: format must be a non-NULL printf-style format string; variadic arguments must match the format.
level should be one of LOG_NONE, LOG_OUTPUT, LOG_ERROR, LOG_WARNING, LOG_TRACE, or LOG_DEBUG.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unspecified; callers should avoid concurrent calls unless the logger guarantees safety.

functions.name: avr_global_logger_set
functions.description: Sets a global logging function to replace the default logger used by avr_global_logger().
requirements: logger must be a valid function pointer of type avr_logger_p (passing NULL behavior is unspecified).
Should be called before logging to ensure messages use the custom logger.

functions.name: avr_global_logger_get
functions.description: Returns the current global logger function pointer.
requirements: None.

functions.name: avr_callback_sleep_gdb
functions.description: Sleep callback used in GDB mode. Typically assigned to avr->sleep to integrate with GDB event processing while delaying for howLong cycles.
requirements: avr must be initialized.
howLong is the number of cycles to sleep; mapping from cycles to real time depends on avr->frequency.
Intended for use when GDB server is active.

functions.name: avr_callback_run_gdb
functions.description: Run callback used in GDB mode. Typically assigned to avr->run to execute instructions while handling GDB events.
requirements: avr must be initialized.
Intended to be used when GDB server is active.

functions.name: avr_callback_sleep_raw
functions.description: Sleep callback for raw mode (no GDB). Usually calls into the host sleep for an accumulated time based on howLong cycles.
requirements: avr must be initialized.
howLong is the number of cycles to sleep; conversion depends on avr->frequency.

functions.name: avr_callback_run_raw
functions.description: Run callback for raw mode (no GDB). Executes instructions as fast as possible without GDB overhead.
requirements: avr must be initialized.

functions.name: avr_pending_sleep_usec
functions.description: Accumulates sleep requests and returns 0 until a minimum threshold of requested microseconds is reached; used by sleep callbacks to coalesce small sleeps.
requirements: avr must be initialized.
howLong is a cycle count to add; conversion to microseconds depends on avr->frequency.
Return value is the sleep time in microseconds once the minimum is reached; exact threshold is unspecified.

functions.name: avr_get_time_stamp
functions.description: Returns the number of real-time microseconds elapsed since the simulation started.
requirements: avr must be initialized.

functions.name: avr_where
functions.description: Returns a text description of the current flash location pointed to by the AVR’s PC. Requires CONFIG_SIMAVR_TRACE to be enabled.
requirements: avr must be initialized.
Only valid/meaningful when the simulator is built with CONFIG_SIMAVR_TRACE; otherwise behavior or return value may be undefined or NULL.
Returned pointer is valid as a const string owned by the simulator; do not free.

functions.name: avr_register_io
functions.description: Registers an IO module with the given AVR instance so its reset/ioctl/dealloc hooks participate in the simulation lifecycle. Typically called by the AVR core during initialization; external modules may also register after instantiation.
requirements: avr must point to a valid, initialized avr_t instance.
io must point to a valid avr_io_t whose fields are properly initialized (at minimum, io->avr either NULL or set; io->reset/io->ioctl/io->dealloc may be NULL if unused).
Should be called after the AVR instance is created and before relying on the IO module’s behavior.
Not re-entrant; do not call concurrently with other IO chain mutations.

functions.name: avr_io_setirqs
functions.signature: avr_irq_t * avr_io_setirqs(avr_io_t * io, uint32_t ctl, int count, avr_irq_t * irqs );
functions.description: Configures the official IRQs exposed by an IO module and the ioctl selector used to retrieve them. If irqs is NULL, an array of count IRQs is allocated and returned; otherwise the provided irqs array is used.
requirements: io must be a valid avr_io_t associated with an AVR (io->avr set).
ctl is the ioctl selector the module will recognize for IRQ retrieval (commonly built with AVR_IOCTL_DEF); exact values are module-specific.
If irqs is NULL, count must be > 0 to allow allocation; the returned pointer becomes owned by the module and will be freed on deallocation.
If irqs is non-NULL, it must reference an array with at least count elements, valid for the lifetime of the IO module.
count must be >= 0; index ranges when later querying are [0, count).
Must be called before external code attempts to fetch the module’s IRQs via avr_io_getirq/avr_ioctl.

functions.name: avr_register_io_read
functions.signature: void avr_register_io_read(avr_t *avr, avr_io_addr_t addr, avr_io_read_t read, void * param);
functions.description: Registers a callback invoked when the IO register at address addr is read by the simulated AVR. The callback can tailor the returned value and side effects.
requirements: avr must be a valid, initialized avr_t instance.
addr must be a valid IO address for the target AVR; behavior is undefined for out-of-range addresses.
read must be a valid function pointer of type avr_io_read_t; it will be called on IO reads at addr.
param is an opaque user pointer passed to the callback; may be NULL.
Callback must be prepared to be called from the simulator execution context and avoid long blocking operations.

functions.name: avr_register_io_write
functions.signature: void avr_register_io_write(avr_t *avr, avr_io_addr_t addr, avr_io_write_t write, void * param);
functions.description: Registers a callback invoked when the IO register at address addr is written by the simulated AVR. The callback is responsible for performing the actual write to the simulated memory/register.
requirements: avr must be a valid, initialized avr_t instance.
addr must be a valid IO address for the target AVR; behavior is undefined for out-of-range addresses.
write must be a valid function pointer of type avr_io_write_t; it will be called on IO writes at addr.
The write callback must perform the memory/register update itself (per header comment).
param is an opaque user pointer passed to the callback; may be NULL.
Callback must be prepared to be called from the simulator execution context and avoid long blocking operations.

functions.name: avr_ioctl
functions.signature: int avr_ioctl(avr_t *avr, uint32_t ctl, void * io_param);
functions.description: Broadcasts an IO control request to all registered IO modules until one handles it. Used to access module-specific features and query/set properties using module-defined control codes.
requirements: avr must be a valid, initialized avr_t instance with IO modules registered.
ctl must be a valid control code understood by one of the modules (typically created via AVR_IOCTL_DEF).
io_param is a module-defined parameter pointer; its type, required initialization, and in/out semantics depend on ctl and the target module (unknown without module docs).
Caller must check the return value to determine success/failure; exact return convention is module-specific (unknown).

functions.name: avr_io_getirq
functions.signature: struct avr_irq_t * avr_io_getirq(avr_t * avr, uint32_t ctl, int index);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a specific IRQ exposed by an IO module identified by ctl, at the given index. This is a convenience wrapper around module IRQ discovery (e.g., via ioctl).
requirements: avr must be a valid, initialized avr_t instance.
ctl must match the module’s irq_ioctl_get value configured via avr_io_setirqs for that module.
index must be within the module’s IRQ range [0, irq_count).
Returns NULL if the module or index is invalid; caller must handle NULL.

functions.name: avr_iomem_getirq
functions.signature: avr_irq_t * avr_iomem_getirq(avr_t * avr, avr_io_addr_t addr, const char * name /* Optional, if NULL, "ioXXXX" will be used */ , int index);
functions.description: Obtains an IRQ hook associated with a specific IO memory address and bit. Enables tracing or reacting to changes on an IO register without module-specific knowledge. If name is NULL, a default name like "ioXXXX" is used.
requirements: avr must be a valid, initialized avr_t instance.
addr must be a valid IO address for the target AVR.
index must be 0..7 for a specific bit, or AVR_IOMEM_IRQ_ALL (8) to monitor all bits (per header macro and comment).
name may be NULL; otherwise should point to a NUL-terminated string persistent for as long as the IRQ exists.
Returned avr_irq_t* may be NULL if the address is invalid or resources cannot be created; caller must handle NULL.

functions.name: avr_deallocate_ios
functions.description: Terminates all IO modules attached to the given AVR, freeing resources and removing them from the IO chain.
requirements: avr must be a valid avr_t instance; safe to call during teardown/shutdown of the simulator.
After this call, previously obtained pointers to module data or IRQs may become invalid; do not use them.
Not re-entrant; do not call concurrently with other IO chain operations.

functions.name: avr_alloc_irq
functions.signature: avr_irq_t * avr_alloc_irq(avr_irq_pool_t * pool, uint32_t base, uint32_t count, const char ** names /* optional */);
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a contiguous block of 'count' IRQs belonging to 'pool'. Each allocated IRQ is assigned an increasing numeric id starting from 'base', and optional human-readable names may be provided. The returned pointer is the first irq in the allocated block; the block should later be released with avr_free_irq. Intended for modules to create their IRQ endpoints before hooks are registered.
requirements: pool must be a valid, initialized pointer to an avr_irq_pool_t that will own the IRQs.
count must be greater than 0.
If names is non-NULL, it must point to an array of at least 'count' valid C strings (one per IRQ).
The returned pointer is valid for at least 'count' consecutive avr_irq_t entries.
Call avr_free_irq(irq, count) to release the block allocated by this function; do not free it by other means.
Register IRQ notify hooks only after module initialization (e.g., in reset handlers), as IRQ registration order is otherwise unspecified.

functions.name: avr_free_irq
functions.description: Frees a contiguous block of 'count' IRQs previously allocated by avr_alloc_irq, invalidating the block starting at 'irq'.
requirements: irq must be a pointer previously returned by avr_alloc_irq (to the first element of the allocated block).
count must match the number of IRQs originally allocated for this block.
After this call, the 'irq' block and its 'count' entries must not be used.
Do not call on IRQs that were not allocated via avr_alloc_irq.

functions.name: avr_init_irq
functions.signature: void avr_init_irq(avr_irq_pool_t * pool, avr_irq_t * irq, uint32_t base, uint32_t count, const char ** names /* optional */);
functions.description: Initializes an existing array of 'count' IRQ descriptors to belong to 'pool', assigning ids starting at 'base' and optional names. This is the non-allocating counterpart to avr_alloc_irq, for callers that manage the storage themselves.
requirements: pool must be a valid, initialized pointer to an avr_irq_pool_t.
irq must point to an array containing at least 'count' writable avr_irq_t elements.
count must be greater than 0.
If names is non-NULL, it must point to an array of at least 'count' valid C strings (one per IRQ).
Callers must ensure initialization occurs before any use, connection, or hook registration on these IRQs.
Register IRQ notify hooks only after module initialization (e.g., in reset handlers) to avoid race conditions.

functions.name: avr_irq_get_flags
functions.description: Returns the current bitmask of IRQ flags (IRQ_FLAG_* constants) for the specified IRQ.
requirements: irq must be a valid, initialized pointer to an avr_irq_t.
The returned flags reflect the current state; callers should not assume any particular initial value unless they have just initialized the IRQ.

functions.name: avr_irq_set_flags
functions.description: Sets the bitmask of IRQ flags (IRQ_FLAG_* constants) on the specified IRQ, affecting behavior such as polarity, filtering, and floating status handling.
requirements: irq must be a valid, initialized pointer to an avr_irq_t.
flags is a bitmask composed of IRQ_FLAG_* values defined in this header.
If IRQ_FLAG_FILTERED is set, notifications are not emitted when the raised value is unchanged from the previous value.
IRQ_FLAG_NOT inverts the IRQ polarity; callers should set flags consistently with how their module interprets values.

functions.name: avr_raise_irq
functions.description: Raises the specified IRQ with the provided value: updates the IRQ's current value, notifies all registered hooks, and propagates to any IRQs connected via chaining. Hook invocation order is undefined.
requirements: irq must be a valid, initialized pointer to an avr_irq_t.
value is a 32-bit value whose semantics are defined by the IRQ provider/module.
Do not rely on the order in which notify hooks are called; the calling order is unspecified.
If IRQ_FLAG_FILTERED is set on this IRQ, notifications will be skipped when the value is unchanged from the previous raise.

functions.name: avr_raise_irq_float
functions.signature: void avr_raise_irq_float(avr_irq_t * irq, uint32_t value, int floating);
functions.description: Raises the IRQ with the provided value and explicitly sets the floating status for the signal. Behaves like avr_raise_irq but also updates whether the signal is considered floating (e.g., no driver).
requirements: irq must be a valid, initialized pointer to an avr_irq_t.
value is a 32-bit value whose semantics are defined by the IRQ provider/module.
floating is treated as boolean (0 = not floating, non-zero = floating).
Do not rely on the order in which notify hooks are called; the calling order is unspecified.
If IRQ_FLAG_FILTERED is set on this IRQ, notifications will be skipped when the value is unchanged from the previous raise.

functions.name: avr_connect_irq
functions.description: Connects a source IRQ to a destination IRQ so that when 'src' is raised, 'dst' is also raised (chained). Used to link components or signals within the simulator.
requirements: src and dst must be valid, initialized pointers to avr_irq_t belonging to appropriate pools/modules.
Call only after both IRQs have been created/initialized.
Do not rely on any particular ordering of notifications relative to other hooks; chaining order is unspecified.
If multiple connections are established, behavior with duplicates is not documented; callers should avoid creating duplicate connections unless the implementation explicitly handles them.

functions.name: avr_unconnect_irq
functions.description: Removes a previously established connection between source and destination IRQs, stopping propagation from 'src' to 'dst'.
requirements: src and dst must be valid, initialized pointers to avr_irq_t.
Should correspond to a prior avr_connect_irq call between the same 'src' and 'dst'.
Safe to call when cleaning up before freeing or reinitializing IRQs.

functions.name: avr_irq_register_notify
functions.signature: void avr_irq_register_notify(avr_irq_t * irq, avr_irq_notify_t notify, void * param);
functions.description: Registers a notification callback (hook) to be called whenever the specified IRQ is raised. The callback receives the IRQ pointer, the raised value, and the user-supplied param. Duplicate registrations of the same hook on the same IRQ are filtered out. Hooks should be registered during reset() handlers, after all modules' init() have run, to avoid initialization-order races.
requirements: irq must be a valid, initialized pointer to an avr_irq_t.
notify must be a valid function pointer matching avr_irq_notify_t.
param is an opaque pointer passed back to the callback; it may be NULL.
The same notify/param pair will not be registered twice on the same IRQ (duplicates are filtered).
Register hooks in reset() handlers (i.e., after all modules' init() functions) to prevent race conditions.
Do not rely on the invocation order of multiple hooks; it is unspecified.

functions.name: avr_irq_unregister_notify
functions.signature: void avr_irq_unregister_notify(avr_irq_t * irq, avr_irq_notify_t notify, void * param);
functions.description: Unregisters a previously registered notification callback for the given IRQ. The notify function and param identify the hook to remove.
requirements: irq must be a valid, initialized pointer to an avr_irq_t.
notify must be the same function pointer that was previously registered for this IRQ.
param should match the param used during registration to uniquely identify the hook to remove.
Should be called before freeing or reinitializing data structures that the callback might reference.

functions.name: avr_register_vector
functions.signature: void avr_register_vector(struct avr_t * avr, avr_int_vector_t * vector);
functions.description: Registers an interrupt vector with the AVR instance so its raised/enable flags can be tracked and IRQs exposed. Typically used when the vector has associated IO register bits (enable/raised) and you want the core to manage/trace them.
requirements: avr must be a valid, initialized AVR core instance.
vector must be a valid pointer to an avr_int_vector_t describing a hardware interrupt vector for this AVR.
vector->vector must not be 0 (vector number 0 is reserved for reset).
Call before raising/servicing this vector if you rely on the 'raised' flag handling or IRQ tracing.

functions.name: avr_raise_interrupt
functions.signature: int avr_raise_interrupt(struct avr_t * avr, avr_int_vector_t * vector);
functions.description: Latches (schedules) an interrupt for the given vector if it is enabled. The interrupt will be serviced later by the core. Returns non-zero if the interrupt was successfully raised and is now pending.
requirements: avr must be a valid AVR core instance.
vector must be a valid interrupt vector for the given AVR.
The vector’s enable flag must be set for the interrupt to be latched (as implied by the comment).
If the vector relies on a 'raised' flag, it should have been registered via avr_register_vector to track it correctly.

functions.name: avr_has_pending_interrupts
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the AVR core currently has any pending interrupts.
requirements: avr must be a valid AVR core instance.

functions.name: avr_is_interrupt_pending
functions.signature: int avr_is_interrupt_pending(struct avr_t * avr, avr_int_vector_t * vector);
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the specified interrupt vector is currently pending for the AVR core.
requirements: avr must be a valid AVR core instance.
vector must be a valid interrupt vector associated with avr.

functions.name: avr_clear_interrupt
functions.signature: void avr_clear_interrupt(struct avr_t * avr, avr_int_vector_t * vector);
functions.description: Clears the pending status of the given interrupt vector.
requirements: avr must be a valid AVR core instance.
vector must be a valid interrupt vector associated with avr.

functions.name: avr_service_interrupts
functions.description: Checks and services pending interrupts. Intended to be called by the core each cycle to dispatch interrupts according to priority and state.
requirements: avr must be a valid AVR core instance.
Call from the core’s execution loop; typically once per emulated CPU cycle as implied by the comment.
Should be called after avr_interrupt_init has been performed.

functions.name: avr_interrupt_reti
functions.description: Notifies the interrupt controller that a RETI instruction was executed by the core, allowing it to update running/pending state and nested interrupt stack.
requirements: avr must be a valid AVR core instance.
Call when the core executes RETI; typically only by the CPU emulation.

functions.name: avr_clear_interrupt_if
functions.signature: int avr_clear_interrupt_if(struct avr_t * avr, avr_int_vector_t * vector, uint8_t old);
functions.description: Clears the interrupt (including pending state) if the vector’s 'raised' flag is set. Returns an int (non-zero on clear). The old parameter is expected to be the prior value of the IO register containing the 'raised' bit.
requirements: avr must be a valid AVR core instance.
vector must be a valid interrupt vector with a defined 'raised' regbit.
old should be the previously read value of the IO register that contains the 'raised' flag for this vector (so the function can test that bit).
The vector should have been registered via avr_register_vector if 'raised' flag handling is needed.

functions.name: avr_get_interrupt_irq
functions.signature: avr_irq_t * avr_get_interrupt_irq(struct avr_t * avr, uint8_t v);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the IRQ that is raised when a vector is enabled and when it is called/cleared, enabling tracing of pending interrupts. v specifies the vector number, or AVR_INT_ANY (0xFF) to get an aggregate/any interrupt IRQ as per the comment.
requirements: avr must be a valid AVR core instance.
v must be a valid vector number for this AVR, or AVR_INT_ANY (0xFF) as a special value.
The corresponding vector should be registered if its IRQs are to be traced.
Caller must handle a possible NULL return if the vector index is invalid or not available (inferred).

functions.name: avr_interrupt_init
functions.description: Initializes the interrupt table for the AVR core.
requirements: avr must be a valid AVR core instance.
Call before using other interrupt helper functions (e.g., registering vectors, raising or servicing interrupts).

functions.name: avr_interrupt_reset
functions.description: Resets the interrupt table and the pending FIFO for the AVR core.
requirements: avr must be a valid AVR core instance.
Safe to call after avr_interrupt_init to clear all pending/running interrupt state.

functions.name: avr_cmd_set_register
functions.signature: void avr_cmd_set_register(struct avr_t * avr, avr_io_addr_t addr);
functions.description: Associates an AVR I/O address with the command-dispatch mechanism so that writes to that register are routed to registered command handlers. Typically called by avr_set_command_register() during device setup. Use this to set which I/O register triggers command callbacks.
requirements: avr must be a valid, initialized pointer to an avr_t instance (initialized via avr_cmd_init/avr_init).
addr must be a valid I/O address for the target AVR (type avr_io_addr_t).
Call before attempting to trigger command handlers via writes to the command I/O register.
This function has no return value; it does not report errors.

functions.name: avr_cmd_register
functions.signature: void avr_cmd_register(struct avr_t * avr, uint8_t code, avr_cmd_handler_t handler, void * param);
functions.description: Registers a command handler for a specific 8-bit command code. When the configured command I/O register is written with that code, the handler is invoked with the written value and the provided param. If the handler returns non-zero, the command is treated as multi-byte and subsequent writes are dispatched to the same handler until it returns 0.
requirements: avr must be a valid, initialized pointer to an avr_t instance (initialized via avr_cmd_init/avr_init).
code is an 8-bit command identifier (range 0–255 by type).
handler must be a valid function pointer of type avr_cmd_handler_t; it will be called with (avr, value_written, param). Passing NULL is not supported (behavior unspecified).
If implementing a multi-byte command, the handler must return non-zero while more bytes are expected and return 0 when the command sequence completes, to release the pending state.
The command table capacity is limited to MAX_AVR_COMMANDS (32); do not register more than this number of commands. Behavior when exceeding the limit is unspecified.
To have the handler invoked, a command I/O register must have been set via avr_cmd_set_register (typically done by avr_set_command_register).
This function has no return value; it does not report errors.
Uniqueness and overwrite behavior for duplicate code registrations are not documented (behavior unspecified).

functions.name: avr_cmd_unregister
functions.signature: void avr_cmd_unregister(struct avr_t * avr, uint8_t code);
functions.description: Unregisters the command handler previously associated with the specified 8-bit command code, disabling dispatch for that code on subsequent writes to the command I/O register.
requirements: avr must be a valid, initialized pointer to an avr_t instance.
code is an 8-bit command identifier (range 0–255 by type).
This function has no return value; it does not report errors.
Behavior when unregistering a code that was not registered or is currently pending as part of a multi-byte command is not documented (behavior unspecified).

functions.name: avr_cycle_timer_register
functions.signature: void avr_cycle_timer_register(struct avr_t *avr, avr_cycle_count_t when, avr_cycle_timer_t timer, void *param)
functions.description: Registers a one-shot cycle timer callback to be invoked after a specified number of cycles. Schedules the callback 'timer' to run in 'when' cycles relative to the current CPU cycle count of the provided AVR instance. The callback is called when the scheduled cycle is reached (or later, if there is lag). If the callback returns 0 the timer is cleared; if it returns a non-zero cycle count, the timer is rescheduled accordingly. Intended for scheduling work within the simulator's cycle-accurate event loop.
requirements: avr must point to a valid, initialized struct avr_t associated with a running/steppable simulator instance.
timer must be a valid function pointer of type avr_cycle_timer_t; it will be called with (avr, when_abs, param).
param may be NULL or any pointer; it is passed through to the callback and used to identify/cancel/status the timer.
when is a cycle count offset (relative delay) and may be zero or greater; exact range is unknown from this header.

Callbacks may be invoked later than the exact target cycle and may be called repeatedly to catch up if there was lag; the callback must be able to handle being called multiple times and should be fast/non-blocking.
The timer pool has a maximum of 64 slots per AVR instance (MAX_CYCLE_TIMERS); exceeding concurrent active timers may fail or drop registrations (exact behavior not specified).
The pair (timer, param) is used for cancellation/status queries; ensure consistency when calling related APIs.

functions.name: avr_cycle_timer_register_usec
functions.signature: void avr_cycle_timer_register_usec(struct avr_t *avr, uint32_t when, avr_cycle_timer_t timer, void *param)
functions.description: Registers a one-shot timer to be invoked after a specified number of microseconds. Schedules the callback 'timer' to run after 'when' microseconds based on the AVR's clock settings. The callback behavior mirrors avr_cycle_timer_register: returning 0 clears the timer; returning a non-zero cycle count reschedules it.
requirements: avr must point to a valid, initialized struct avr_t tied to a configured clock so that usec-to-cycles conversion is meaningful.
timer must be a valid avr_cycle_timer_t function pointer; it will be called with the absolute cycle at which it fires and the provided param.
param may be NULL or any pointer payload; it is used to identify/cancel/status the timer as well.
when is a microsecond delay; valid range is unknown from this header; very large values may overflow internal conversion depending on clock and types (not specified).
Callbacks may be invoked later than the exact target time and may be called repeatedly to catch up; the callback must tolerate repeated invocations and be fast/non-blocking.
Subject to the same 64-slot maximum concurrent timers per AVR instance (MAX_CYCLE_TIMERS).
Use the same (timer, param) when calling cancel/status for this timer.

functions.name: avr_cycle_timer_cancel
functions.signature: void avr_cycle_timer_cancel(struct avr_t *avr, avr_cycle_timer_t timer, void *param)
functions.description: Cancels a previously registered cycle timer identified by the function pointer and parameter pair. If a matching timer is pending, it is removed from the active queue so it will not fire.
requirements: avr must point to a valid, initialized struct avr_t.
timer must be the same function pointer that was used when registering the timer to cancel.
param must match the param used at registration to uniquely identify the timer instance.
If no matching timer exists, the call is a no-op; specific return/indication is not provided (function returns void).
Behavior with multiple pending timers sharing the same (timer, param) is unspecified in this header.

functions.name: avr_cycle_timer_status
functions.signature: avr_cycle_count_t avr_cycle_timer_status(struct avr_t *avr, avr_cycle_timer_t timer, void *param)
functions.description: Queries whether a specific timer is pending and, if so, returns the remaining cycles until it fires plus one; returns 0 if no such timer is present. The timer is identified by the function pointer and parameter pair used at registration.
requirements: avr must point to a valid, initialized struct avr_t.
timer must be the same callback pointer used during registration of the timer being queried.
param must match the param used at registration; the pair (timer, param) identifies the timer.
Return value semantics: 0 means no matching timer; non-zero is the number of cycles remaining plus one as documented.

functions.name: strsep
functions.description: Tokenizes a mutable C string in-place by replacing the next delimiter with a NUL and advancing *stringp to the next position. This is a BSD/Glibc-style utility exposed here for MinGW builds. Typical usage: iterate calling strsep(&p, ", ") to split a line. Returns a pointer to the current token or NULL when no tokens remain. Available only when compiled with __MINGW32__ defined.
requirements: Available only when __MINGW32__ is defined (per header guard).
stringp must be a non-NULL pointer to a char* variable; *stringp may be NULL to indicate no more tokens.
*stringp must point to a writable, NUL-terminated string buffer because the function writes NUL terminators in-place.
delim must be a non-NULL pointer to a NUL-terminated string listing delimiter characters.
The lifetime of the underlying buffer referenced by *stringp must outlive all token uses since tokens alias the same buffer.
On each call, *stringp will be updated to point past the token (or set to NULL at end); callers must observe the updated value.
Return value is the token pointer on success or NULL when no more tokens are available; callers should check for NULL to terminate iteration.

functions.name: argv_parse
functions.description: Parses a mutable command line into words, destructively splitting the line and populating an argv_t with argc and argv pointers to each word. The input line is also stripped of trailing CR/LF characters. You may pass a previously allocated argv_t to be reused and grown as needed, or NULL to allocate a new one. No duplication of the line text is performed; argv entries point into the provided line buffer.
requirements: line must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable, NUL-terminated buffer; the function modifies it by inserting NULs to split words.
The memory backing line must remain valid for as long as any argv pointers are accessed, since no copies are made.
argv may be NULL (to allocate a new argv_t) or a valid pointer to an existing argv_t previously allocated for reuse; the function may grow it to fit.
Caller is responsible for freeing the returned argv_t when no longer needed.
Caller is responsible for freeing the line buffer if it was dynamically allocated by the caller (no duplication is made).
The function strips any \r and \n from the line as part of parsing.
Error reporting and return-on-failure behavior are not documented; callers should treat a NULL return as an allocation or parsing failure (inferred due to allocator semantics).

functions.name: sim_setup_firmware
functions.signature: void sim_setup_firmware(const char * filename, uint32_t loadBase, struct elf_firmware_t * fp, const char * progname);
functions.description: Loads a firmware file (ELF or Intel HEX) into an elf_firmware_t structure, preparing it for use by the simulator. The filename selects the input image; loadBase is the base address for HEX loads; fp is populated with the parsed/loaded firmware; progname is used for error reporting. Usage: call once per firmware to initialize fp prior to running the simulator. Notes: Exact behavior for progname==NULL or how loadBase is used for ELF images is not documented; details of elf_firmware_t population are internal to simavr.
requirements: filename must be a valid, non-null C string path to an existing readable firmware file in ELF or Intel HEX format.
fp must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable struct elf_firmware_t to receive results.
loadBase is used as the base of the load region for HEX input; behavior for ELF images is not specified in this header.
progname should be a valid C string used in error messages; behavior if NULL is not specified.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for an "alphanumeric string" representing an MCU name supported by simavr.
# The fuzzer stub tries two curated names and then a random string. To maximize successful
# avr_make_mcu_by_name calls, we return a valid known MCU name most of the time, while
# occasionally returning plausible alternatives or slight variations to exercise alias/lookup paths.

KNOWN_NAMES: List[str] = [
    # Common AVR MCUs likely built in various simavr configs
    "mega328", "mega32u4", "mega88", "mega16", "mega128",
    "mega2560", "mega1284", "mega168", "tiny85", "tiny13",
    "tiny24", "tiny44", "tiny84", "tiny25", "tiny45",
    "tiny2313", "tiny1634", "mega64m1", "mega16m1", "mega324a",
    # Add a few more common aliases/devices found in simavr trees
    "mega8", "mega32", "mega48", "mega169p", "mega644", "mega1281",
    "mega328pb", "mega1280", "mega128rfa1", "mega128rfr2", "usb162",
]

# Some deliberate variants that are still valid for certain builds or exercise parsing
VALID_VARIANTS: List[str] = [
    # Case variants and underscores shouldn't matter if lookup is case-sensitive; keep valid
    # We keep only known-good lowercase to maximize success; include select with suffixes
    "atmega328p",  # common alias sometimes supported
    "atmega32u4",
    "atmega88",
    "attiny85",
    "attiny13",
    "attiny2313",
]

# Fallback plausible random alphanumeric string resembling an AVR model
def random_model_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    fam = rng.choice(["mega", "tiny", "atmega", "attiny"])  # common families
    num = rng.choice([8, 16, 32, 48, 64, 88, 128, 168, 169, 256, 324, 328])
    suffix = rng.choice(["", "p", "pb", "u4", "m1", "a", "rfa1", "rfr2"])
    return f"{fam}{num}{suffix}"

# The main generate function emits bytes for FUZZ_PARAM_STR to consume.
# We bias towards KNOWN_NAMES to ensure the first two candidate attempts in the stub succeed.

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Strategy probabilities:
    #  - 75%: pick a KNOWN_NAMES entry directly
    #  - 15%: pick a VALID_VARIANTS alias
    #  - 10%: synthesize a plausible model-like string
    p = rng.random()
    if p < 0.75:
        s = rng.choice(KNOWN_NAMES)
    elif p < 0.90:
        s = rng.choice(VALID_VARIANTS)
    else:
        s = random_model_like(rng)

    # Ensure strictly alphanumeric/underscore per data type description
    allowed = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"
    s = "".join(ch for ch in s if ch in allowed)
    # Bound total length; fuzzer buffer should be modest
    s = s[:64]

    # Return as bytes
    return s.encode("ascii", errors="ignore")

import os
import random
from typing import List

# This generator targets stubs that consume raw bytes via FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# Goals:
# - Produce diverse but valid blobs for avr_loadcode (flash code bytes), read_hex_string source, and hdump buffer.
# - Keep size <= 1024 for avr_loadcode stub (it mods by 1024) and generally <= 4096 overall.
# - Include patterns that may exercise different simulator behaviors (e.g., NOPs, jumps, interrupts, mixed data).

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

# Useful AVR opcode-like byte patterns (not required to be valid opcodes everywhere, but realistic):
NOP = b"\x00\x00"              # NOP (word)
RJMP = b"\x00\xC0"             # RJMP k (placeholder word with k=0)
RET = b"\x08\x95"               # RET
RETI = b"\x18\x95"              # RETI
WDR = b"\xA8\x95"               # WDR
SLEEP = b"\x88\x95"             # SLEEP
BREAK = b"\x98\x95"             # BREAK
SEI = b"\x78\x94"               # SEI
CLI = b"\xF8\x94"               # CLI

# Some filler patterns
PAT_ZERO = b"\x00" * 32
PAT_FF = b"\xFF" * 32
PAT_INC = bytes([i & 0xFF for i in range(64)])
PAT_DEC = bytes([(255 - i) & 0xFF for i in range(64)])

# Construct small code-like sequences (words are little-endian in flash array, but we just provide bytes)
SEQ_BOOT = SEI + CLI + NOP + NOP
SEQ_ISR = SEI + RETI
SEQ_IDLE = NOP * 8 + SLEEP + NOP * 8
SEQ_MISC = WDR + BREAK + RET

# Common ASCII blocks for read_hex_string -> hex conversion variety
ASCII_BLOCKS = [
    b"Hello, AVR!",
    b"\x00\x01\x02binary\x7F\x80\xFF",
    b"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog",
    b"\xFF" * 50,
    bytes(range(0, 32)),
]


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _mix_parts(rng: random.Random, parts: List[bytes], target_len: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    # Shuffle and append until reaching target length
    pool = parts[:]
    rng.shuffle(pool)
    i = 0
    while len(out) < target_len:
        if not pool:
            pool = parts[:]
            rng.shuffle(pool)
            i = 0
        chunk = pool[i % len(pool)]
        i += 1
        # Optionally slice chunk to add variability
        if len(chunk) > 0 and rng.random() < 0.5:
            start = rng.randrange(0, len(chunk))
            end = rng.randrange(start + 1, len(chunk) + 1)
            chunk = chunk[start:end]
        out.extend(chunk)
    return bytes(out[:target_len])


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide an overall length. Keep <= 2048 to be safe and fast.
    total_len = rng.randint(128, min(2048, MAX_TOTAL))

    # Build a "flash code" region sized <= 1024 (avr_loadcode stub uses size % 1024)
    flash_len = rng.randint(16, min(1024, total_len // 2))

    flash_parts = [
        PAT_ZERO[:rng.randint(0, len(PAT_ZERO))],
        PAT_FF[:rng.randint(0, len(PAT_FF))],
        PAT_INC[:rng.randint(0, len(PAT_INC))],
        PAT_DEC[:rng.randint(0, len(PAT_DEC))],
        SEQ_BOOT,
        SEQ_ISR,
        SEQ_IDLE,
        SEQ_MISC,
        RJMP * rng.randint(0, 4),
        _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, 64)),
    ]
    flash_blob = _mix_parts(rng, flash_parts, flash_len)

    # Build a general blob for read_hex_string/hdump scenarios with mixed ASCII and binary
    rest_len = max(0, total_len - flash_len)
    textish = rng.choice(ASCII_BLOCKS)
    general_parts = [
        textish,
        _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(8, 128)),
        bytes(reversed(textish)),
        b"\r\n\t " * rng.randint(0, 8),
        bytes([0x00]) * rng.randint(0, 32),
        bytes([0xFF]) * rng.randint(0, 32),
        bytes(range(256)) if rest_len > 512 and rng.random() < 0.3 else b"",
    ]
    general_parts = [p for p in general_parts if p]
    rest_blob = _mix_parts(rng, general_parts, rest_len)

    # Concatenate; the fuzzer will draw FUZZ_PARAM_STR independently, but giving a single buffer
    # with multiple interesting regions increases chance of exercising different code paths when
    # the framework slices from it.
    return flash_blob + rest_blob

import random
from typing import List

# Intel HEX generator for valid minimal firmware images
# Targets fuzzers sim_setup_firmware and read_ihex_file which expect a valid IHEX file on disk.
# We return the bytes content for such a file.

HEX_CHARS = "0123456789ABCDEF"

def _hex_byte(v: int) -> str:
    v &= 0xFF
    return HEX_CHARS[(v >> 4) & 0xF] + HEX_CHARS[v & 0xF]

def _record(byte_count: int, address: int, rectype: int, data: bytes) -> str:
    # Build an IHEX record string including checksum and trailing newline
    # :LL AAAA TT [data...] CC\n
    ll = byte_count & 0xFF
    addr_hi = (address >> 8) & 0xFF
    addr_lo = address & 0xFF
    tt = rectype & 0xFF

    # Checksum is two's complement of sum of ll, addr_hi, addr_lo, tt, and data bytes
    checksum = (-(ll + addr_hi + addr_lo + tt + sum(data)) & 0xFF)

    s = [":", _hex_byte(ll), _hex_byte(addr_hi), _hex_byte(addr_lo), _hex_byte(tt)]
    s.extend(_hex_byte(b) for b in data)
    s.append(_hex_byte(checksum))
    s.append("\n")
    return "".join(s)

MCU_NAMES: List[str] = [
    # Common AVR MCU names often recognized by simavr ELF images; may be embedded in extended records
    "atmega328p", "atmega328", "atmega32u4", "atmega2560", "atmega1280",
    "attiny85", "attiny45", "attiny13", "attiny84", "atmega8",
]


def _gen_data_payload(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 32) -> bytes:
    # Generate a small but varied payload: ASCII, random bytes, and pattern mixes
    modes = ["ascii", "rand", "pattern"]
    mode = rng.choice(modes)
    n = rng.randint(1, max_len)
    if mode == "ascii":
        alphabet = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789" \
                   b" _-:/.,\n\r\t"
        return bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))
    elif mode == "pattern":
        # Repeating patterns with boundaries that can exercise decoders
        base = bytes([(i * 37 + 11) & 0xFF for i in range(256)])
        start = rng.randrange(0, 200)
        return (base[start:start + n])
    else:
        return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _make_ihex(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    lines: List[str] = []

    # Optionally add an Extended Linear Address record (type 04) to place data above 64KB
    use_ela = rng.random() < 0.3
    upper = 0
    if use_ela:
        # Choose a small upper word to keep address space reasonable (e.g., 0..3 => up to 0x0003:0xFFFF)
        upper = rng.randrange(0, 4)
        ela_data = bytes([(upper >> 8) & 0xFF, upper & 0xFF])
        lines.append(_record(2, 0x0000, 0x04, ela_data))

    # Optionally add an Extended Segment Address record (type 02); though ELA and ESA shouldn't mix in strict files,
    # many parsers accept either before data. Keep it optional and independent with low probability.
    if not use_ela and rng.random() < 0.15:
        esa = rng.randrange(0, 16)  # 4-bit segment in units of 16 bytes
        esa_data = bytes([(esa >> 8) & 0xFF, esa & 0xFF])
        lines.append(_record(2, 0x0000, 0x02, esa_data))

    # Optionally embed a comment-like record using Start Linear Address (type 05) which some loaders ignore
    # Use a plausible reset vector address 0x00000000 or 0x00000080
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        sla = rng.choice([0x00000000, 0x00000080])
        sla_bytes = bytes([(sla >> 24) & 0xFF, (sla >> 16) & 0xFF, (sla >> 8) & 0xFF, sla & 0xFF])
        lines.append(_record(4, 0x0000, 0x05, sla_bytes))

    # Create 1..3 data records. First one at address 0 to match simple loaders; optional additional records at offsets.
    num_data = rng.randint(1, 3)
    addr = 0x0000
    for i in range(num_data):
        payload = _gen_data_payload(rng)
        # Keep each record within 1..32 bytes
        if len(payload) > 32:
            payload = payload[:32]
        lines.append(_record(len(payload), addr, 0x00, payload))
        # Next record address: either contiguous or a small jump within first 256 bytes
        if i + 1 < num_data:
            if rng.random() < 0.6:
                addr = (addr + len(payload)) & 0xFFFF
            else:
                addr = rng.randrange(0, 256)

    # Mandatory EOF record
    lines.append(_record(0, 0x0000, 0x01, b""))

    return "".join(lines)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # With some probability, generate the simplest possible file (one data record + EOF at addr 0)
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        payload = _gen_data_payload(rng)
        if len(payload) > 32:
            payload = payload[:32]
        ihex = _record(len(payload), 0x0000, 0x00, payload) + _record(0, 0x0000, 0x01, b"")
        return ihex.encode("ascii")

    # Otherwise generate a richer file with optional extended addressing and multiple records
    ihex = _make_ihex(rng)
    # Ensure size limit
    data = ihex.encode("ascii")
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data
